extensionProposals.version: prepared context binding extension on protocol 2; package version to be agreed
extensionProposals.operations: No new wire operation is sent. Published v2 execution and workflow lifecycle schemas remain unchanged; the proposal binds their authenticated custody to PREPARED/1.
extensionProposals.missing: Resolve Maestro principal chains and opaque grantRef into v2 grant UUID/digest references without losing root/parent lineage or narrowing away context. Bind workflowId/version/triggerEventId plus opaque ownerEpoch/fencingToken to the producer-owned ownerId, exact prepared snapshot, actor registration and current connection. Public executionRequestV2 has no workflow owner/fence fields and does not authorize a local spawn; a broker receipt cannot replace this binding.
extensionProposals.localConsumer: ManagedHostAdapterDeps.workflowNegotiation is a trusted host-only read of actual v2 support for the supplied PreparedExecutionPort, cloned protected identity and socket generation. Absent, v1, malformed or incomplete negotiation is unavailable. Delegation requires execution/registration_use/delegation; workflows additionally require all four workflow lifecycle capabilities. Admission sends the existing complete request unchanged, retains the original producer lease and checks negotiation again after admission and at the sink. No producer, wire transport or advertised capability is installed.
extensionProposals.lifetime: The producer must resolve and authenticate every delegation hop/grant and owner fence, reauthorize each attempt, durably reject replay/stale/revoked grants and fence loss, and revoke descendant effects. Changed negotiation or context prevents local use of the lease; lost admission remains unknown. Local fixture tests are not authenticated producer, native or paired qualification.

extensionProposals.version: purpose-bound runtime approval HTTP mapping for registration schema 2
extensionProposals.operations: Existing approve_runtime_registration HTTP body remains v1. Propose a negotiated v2 mapping; no new route is sent.
extensionProposals.missing: Public runtimeApprovalInputV2 exists, but http-operations accepts only challengeId/nonce/challengeDigest. No public session identifier is exposed for consumer-side session correlation; session binding remains server-owned. Never drop purpose/version to fit v1.

extensionProposals.version: new versioned capability on protocol 2; package version to be agreed
extensionProposals.operations: Propose execution_prepare, execution_consume, execution_settle, execution_reconcile; none is shipped.
extensionProposals.localConsumer: EndpointPort.preparedExecution, PreparedExecutionPort.version=1, extends the existing HostAuthority lifetime. admit receives the unchanged AdmissionRequest plus a cloned ManagedIdentityRecord and socket connection generation. Match registered actor/installation, exact snapshot digest, policy revision, trust/registration generation and original producer lease before returning admission; recheck at the sink. No production producer or capability advertisement is installed.
extensionProposals.lifetime: The negotiated producer must durably consume once, pin native executable/resource identities and descendant ownership, revoke on policy/registration/trust/disconnect, and settle/reconcile through its original lease. Local cancellation invalidates pending admission, duplicate attempts are refused, and thrown/lost outcomes remain unknown even after disconnect. In-memory retry fences do not replace producer durable reconciliation after restart.
extensionProposals.publishedSchemas: executionBinding describes trusted resolved handles; executionConsumption is already consumed with unknown outcome; executionCompletion is settlement evidence. None grants a new local effect. Missing transport negotiation and prepare/consume/settle/reconcile mapping remain proposed-not-negotiated.
extensionProposals.missing: Prepare binds registration/delegation/workflow, request/attempt/run, exact argv/env/cwd/resources and digests, provider/model/route/credential, policy/DLP/budget/egress/backend. Return single-use expiring grant/handle and bindingDigest; consume/settle/reconcile preserve durable unknown outcomes and process/descendant ownership.

extensionProposals.version: new versioned capability on protocol 2; package version to be agreed
extensionProposals.operations: Propose effect_authorize, effect_settle, effect_reconcile; none is shipped.
extensionProposals.missing: Exact command/file/permission/tool input plus leaseId, authenticated actor reference, provider/thread/turn/request IDs, effect digest, policy revision, expiry, revocation and idempotency. Correlated allow/deny/unavailable/unknown must remain distinct; a launch/dispatch receipt cannot grant an effect.
extensionProposals.localConsumer: ManagedEffectProducer.version=1 is injected through ManagedHostAdapterDeps.effectProducer only after authenticated negotiation. createManagedEffectAuthority sends a cloned full request plus binding, digest, policy revision and standing generation to authorize, validates its receipt, then consumes once before returning a live-checked allow. No production producer, endpoint operation or advertised capability is installed.
extensionProposals.lifetime: Only an owned bound prepared lease with matching actor/provider and current registration/policy/trust may ask. Lease release/revocation and caller cancellation abort pending requests. Inputs, receipt identity/digest/policy/expiry and standing are rechecked after each await and at the reply sink, including after relay consent. Lost/malformed responses stay unknown; retries and reused receipts are held. In-memory fences do not replace durable producer reconciliation.
extensionProposals.nativeBoundary: The negotiated producer must pin exact native file/executable/network identities, enforce confinement and descendant revocation through the actual effect, and durably settle/reconcile consumption. Receipt consume grants one permission without executing the effect. These obligations are not implemented by the published wire schemas and remain unqualified. Complete provider inputs are preserved; a permission projection alone cannot qualify native confinement.

extensionProposals.version: local delivery extension for desktop-policy schema 1
extensionProposals.operations: Propose desktop_policy, offline_choices and typed ceiling delivery; no corresponding local endpoint operations are published.
extensionProposals.localConsumer: MCOMP-15-01 extends createPolicyStatusService with NativePolicyProjectionPort.version=1, a trusted host-only readVerified port plus the pinned DesktopPolicySchemaPort. The producer must authenticate negotiation and verify signatures over the entire desktop/settings/routes/secondary-ceilings batch against protected identity, registration and trust root before returning. No production producer, wire operation or capability advertisement is installed.
extensionProposals.installation: The consumer reuses desktop-policy schema 1, ManagedRouteCeiling, parseManagedSettingsPolicy and nine existing ceiling parsers. It validates tenant/org/enrollment/installation/actor/runtime/epoch, applied revision, freshness, complete sections and route shape before one atomic in-memory replacement. Connection/trust/registration/source changes and superseded requests are rejected. Same-revision content conflicts, rollback and older projections retain the previous restrictions. Reads return copies scoped to identity/actor/trust; disconnected or expired policy never grants execution, and restart defaults to unavailable until verified refresh. Settings/choice/effect sink composition remains in the dependent implementation tasks.
extensionProposals.missing: Authenticated registration/policy digest and revision, projection freshness, approved provider/model/account/workspace/tool/credential references, and explicit browser/shell/plugin/install/egress/listener/custody constraints. Published UI projection alone cannot authorize host mutations or effects.
extensionProposals.approvedOptions: MCOMP-15-03 returns only bounded opaque desktop references with locks, revision and an expiry bounded by projection, registration and observation freshness. Optional host-only executionChoices binds providerRef to explicit permission modes and opaque transport references, limited to 128 providers and 128 transports each. The whole extension must be signed in the native batch. Missing executionChoices yields unavailable fields, never unrestricted options. Current port, actor/trust/runtime/epoch, connection and applied revision are rechecked on every read. Commit/run must revalidate independently; no producer or wire capability is supplied.
extensionProposals.credentialResolution: MCOMP-15-04 reuses bindApprovedCredentials and buildAgentLaunchPlan. Branded entries are immutable; every launch must supply a fresh host-authenticated credentialConsumer (tenant, actor, agent, applied revision) independent of the reference. Provider, destination and opaque account digest must also match the actual route before secret lookup. Expired/future bindings, unknown routes and unapproved OAuth/env/config/args overrides are held. Credential references and a UI choice are not authority: the public protocol still lacks authenticated reference/source resolution, consumer binding and revocation delivery. No production credential producer or wire capability is supplied; DESKTOP-LOCAL/1 and PREPARED/1 must bind the actual process/sink before production use. Native account-file/keychain isolation and provider behavior remain separate qualification obligations.
extensionProposals.standaloneListeners: MCOMP-21-01 composes the headless Cue engine onto the same leaf listener gate before it binds: buildStandaloneCueListenerAuthority (src/cli/services/cue-standalone-engine.ts) reads the protected installation standing per bind and judges cue-webhook and cue-status with managedListenerStanding and listenerVerdict under the attached host applied revision, else the record revision. No published operation delivers a listener ceiling, so an enrolled, unavailable or unreadable standing refuses both kinds unavailable by name and standalone binds as before. The listener constraint of this batch must reach that consumer before a managed headless engine may open either socket.
extensionProposals.standaloneRepositoryGate: MCOMP-21-01B installs the desktop git execution gate (createGitExecutionGate) in the headless Cue engine before it arms triggers: buildStandaloneCueGitExecutionGate reads the same protected installation standing per hold and judges with managedRepositoryStanding + repositoryEffectVerdict. No published operation delivers a repository ceiling, so a managed standing refuses every GitHub poll (and any git write in that process) unavailable by name; an SSH write is refused remote-unqualified because no remote endpoint qualifier is composed headless. Standalone holds nothing. Repository ceiling delivery remains proposed-not-negotiated.
extensionProposals.standaloneEgressAndCustody: MCOMP-21-02 installs an egress authority (setEgressAuthority) and a credential custody authority (setCredentialCustodyAuthority) in the headless Cue engine before it exists, both read per request from the same protected installation standing and judged with the desktop rules (managedEgressStanding + egressVerdict, headlessCredentialAuthority). The notify webhook names the user-webhook class; SusFactor holds both 0DIN destinations as vendor-telemetry before the token or any input is sent. No published operation delivers an egress ceiling, so a managed standing refuses every outbound request unavailable by name before a socket opens and refuses the ODIN_API_TOKEN environment custody. Standalone holds nothing. Egress ceiling delivery remains proposed-not-negotiated.
extensionProposals.standaloneNotifyWebhookCredential: MCOMP-21-02A holds the credential in the user info of the --notify-webhook URL (cue.notifyWebhookCredential) to the same custody authority before a notification is queued. Its custody is the command line (kind command-line, visible in the process list and the shell history), which credentialCustodyVerdict refuses on a managed standing, so a managed headless engine sends no notification carrying it, logs the [managed-command-line] refusal once and counts held notifications; the credential is never stripped to send anyway. A URL without user info is not held by custody (egress still applies). Standalone unchanged. No published operation delivers a protected credential reference for this flag.
extensionProposals.runtimeHostListener: MCOMP-21-03 gives the detached maestro-cli host bridge its own listener kind, runtime-host (kept apart from web), held at the leaf gate by startRuntimeHost (src/cli/services/runtime-host.ts) after the standing re-attaches and before telemetry, Cue or startRuntimeServer, under runtimeHostListenerAuthority: managedListenerStanding and listenerVerdict over the runtime own binding, read per bind, any state but standalone managed. No published operation delivers a listener ceiling, so an enrolled, enrolled-unavailable or unreadable host refuses unavailable by name (host start LISTENER_HELD, exit 1) and opens no socket; standalone binds 127.0.0.1 as before. Bridge dispatch stays principal-bound by runtimeManagedScope and managedScopeRefusal. MCOMP-21-03A composes the endpoint inbox on the headless host and MCOMP-21-03B its typed command service (composeHostManaged): cancel revokes only leases the runtime own host authority admitted, refresh re-attaches through the same enrollment lifecycle, report names the facts this host holds and lists HOST_COMMAND_REPORT_GAPS (no receipts ledger, contracts pin, providers or subagents read here) instead of zeros; the ledger loads before the dial and decides only under a registered standing. No published producer delivers a command to a runtime (CP-02), so nothing new is advertised.
extensionProposals.tuiHandshakeProducers: MCOMP-21-04 composes the maestro-p admission handshake into the headless producers: stampTuiAdmission() (src/shared/maestro-lib/managed/tui-handshake.ts) signs, with the producer data directory key (never a key carried in the environment), the lease run (lease, authority, attempt, request, run, policy revision), the approved claude binary digest, the permission ceiling and the terminal owner (producer surface and lease actor), and mints a fresh steering token; startTurn adds only TUI_STAMPED_ENV_NAMES after its gate (StartTurnOptions.admission.hostEnv), so the lease digest never names them and no other name rides past the snapshot. The CLI (src/cli/services/agent-spawner.ts) strips an inherited handshake or steering token from every local maestro-p launch and refuses a managed one it cannot sign (policy-denied) instead of letting the omission read as an unmanaged host. The TUI side (readTuiHandshakeEnv, checkTuiSpawn, steeringFrameRefusal) is unchanged. MCOMP-21-04A does the same for Cue prompt runs on the desktop and the standalone engine (src/main/cue/cue-process-lifecycle.ts): every local maestro-p spec drops an inherited handshake or steering token before the authority sees it, and a managed one is stamped after the admission with surface cue, the context request id, the launch plan permission ceiling (SpawnSpec.permissionCeiling) and the key in resolveUserDataDir(); one it cannot sign is the run managed refusal (policy-denied, lease released). Local Maestro wire only; no Mega operation or capability is claimed.
extensionProposals.webAuthTokenCustody: MCOMP-21-05 moves the persistent web link token into service-owned custody: on a managed host the webAuthToken setting keeps only the opaque reference custody:web.authToken, and the token lives in maestro-web-link.json sealed with the OS key store (createCustodyCredentialSlot() in src/main/enterprise/credential-custody.ts, credential web.authToken) together with its owner (tenant/installation of the trusted enrollment record) and a freshness epoch anchored in the OS credential store. A plaintext token is migrated or, when custody refuses, rotated; a token for another owner, a rolled-back copy or a lost anchor opens nothing and is rotated; unenrolled (standalone) a leftover sealed copy is dropped and the plain setting behaves as before. Local Maestro behavior only: no external wire capability is advertised.
extensionProposals.pluginEgressClass: MCOMP-21-12 names an egress class at the two report-listed plugin callers that still fell to the content default (the third, the Cue notify webhook, already names user-webhook since MCOMP-21-02): plugin net.fetch (src/main/plugins/plugin-host-handlers.ts) and the plugin media download (src/main/plugins/plugin-media-tools.ts) are held as plugin (PLUGIN_EGRESS_CLASS), so a managed ceiling that admits content no longer admits a plugin's own request; standalone nothing is consulted and both requests leave exactly as before. Lite peer traffic (pairing transport, paired relay HTTP and WebSocket upgrades) is not yet held at the egress boundary: continuations MCOMP-21-12A and MCOMP-21-12B. No published operation delivers an egress ceiling, so the plugin class is refused unavailable on a managed host until one is negotiated.
extensionProposals.codexLoginCustody: MCOMP-21-06 holds every read of a Codex login (CODEX_HOME/auth.json, credential codex.auth) to the one credential custody authority as plain-file custody: readCodexAuth (src/main/agents/codex-auth.ts) asks holdCredentialCustody before the file is opened and again after the read resolves, so a host that became managed mid-read hands nothing on. A managed standing (any record that is not standalone) refuses with the managed kind and the [managed-plain-file] line: no token, account id or e-mail decoded from the id_token leaves the reader, the quota sampler records authState error (no sign-in offered) and the reset-credit read and redeem return the refusal before any request. An approved account on the egress ceiling is not a reader and does not reopen the file. No published operation delivers a protected, purpose-scoped lease that resolves an approved provider identity inside custody (missing: approved account reference to sealed token resolution, purpose binding for quota-sample / reset-credits-read / reset-credits-consume, revocation delivery), so a managed host polls no Codex account; standalone reads exactly as before. Transcript discovery (getProviderAccountDirs) reads no credential and is unchanged.
extensionProposals.pluginAuthorizationLedger: MCOMP-21-07 holds the acts that create or widen plugin authority to the managed plugin ceiling before the sealed ledger records them: AuthorizationStore.setManagedStanding (src/main/plugins/authorization-ledger.ts) reads the same ManagedPluginStanding the broker reads and ceilingAuthorizationVerdict (src/main/plugins/permission-broker.ts, sharing the entry rule of ceilingVerdict) refuses a consent mint (ManagedPluginAuthorizationError, nothing moves), an allowlist widening (added members only) and a load-time verify (reason managed, consent kept). Revoke, uninstall and narrowing are never held. The trusted publisher keys are the lock key pluginTrustedKeys (MANAGED_SET_LOCK_KEYS in src/shared/managedSettingsLock.ts), pinned as the whole base64 key list; effectiveTrustedKeys replaces the user keys under a pin. No published operation delivers a plugin ceiling (LOCAL_ENDPOINT_OPERATIONS names none), so an enrolled host composed onto this refuses every mint and load as unavailable by name; composition into src/main/index.ts is MCOMP-21-07A.
extensionProposals.agentRecordPersistence: MCOMP-21-08 holds every agent record a renderer, bridge or plugin write persists to the per-provider lock keys agentConfig.customPath, agentConfig.customArgs, agentConfig.customEnvVars, agentConfig.model and agentConfig.reasoningEffort (record fields customPath, customArgs, customEnvVars, customModel, customEffort; SESSION_CONFIG_LOCK_FIELDS): holdAgentRecordWrite (src/main/enterprise/settings-policy.ts) compares each touched record with the stored one and asks holdAgentConfigWrite, the one evaluation the agents:setConfig* handlers and update_session_config meet, for each changed field. sessions:setMany and sessions:setAll (src/main/ipc/handlers/persistence.ts, which also serve the web-desktop bridge) and the plugin host session writer (setPluginSessionsRaw in src/main/index.ts) run it before the store is written: a refused field is put back to the stored value (removed on a new record), the rest of the write (name, tabs, an admitted field) is kept, and the writer receives a sessions:lifecycleSync update whose baseline is what it sent, so its form drops the refused value. No policy revision or lock view carried on a record is read. A provider change is reauthorized by authorizeProviderSwap, not here. The constrained-choice projection a form would offer (G-09) is not delivered by any published operation; until it is, an enrolled desktop with no usable settings policy holds these fields unavailable, as the agents:setConfig* handlers do.
extensionProposals.worktreeCleanupDeletes: MCOMP-21-09 reacquires authority immediately before each later write or delete of the local worktree and Auto Run surfaces instead of inheriting it from the clone, create, removal or admitted Auto Run action that led there. The git:worktreeSetup empty-folder rmdir is held as `git worktree add <path>` at the main repository through the shared executor hold (holdGitCommand) and as the local-effects delete of that path; the git:removeWorktree recursive-delete fallback is held as `git worktree remove --force <path>` at the worktree and as the local-effects delete, both acquired after `worktree remove` failed; git:worktreeCheckout keeps its executor hold right before `git checkout`. Each sink reads a path handle (lstat device and inode, readLocalPathHandle in src/main/enterprise/local-effects-policy.ts) when it examines the path and deletes or checks out only while the path still names that entry (holdDeleteOfHandles, sameLocalPathHandle): a path swapped across the awaits (a symlink planted, a folder moved in, a confirm left open) is left in place and reported as incomplete cleanup; a failed recursive delete is reported as possibly partial. autorun:deleteFolder holds both playbook folders once and removes only the unchanged ones. No published operation delivers the repository or local-effects ceiling (proposed, not negotiated): an enrolled desktop with none refuses these deletes unavailable by name.
extensionProposals.symphonyForkAfterEffects: MCOMP-21-10 reacquires the repository ceiling immediately before each Symphony after-effect instead of inheriting it from the admitted fork, clone or PR operation. ensureForkSetup (src/main/utils/symphony-fork.ts) takes beforeRemoteChange, required whenever beforeFork is given, and calls it fresh before each post-fork command: the origin-to-upstream rename (commit, local: a configuration write, as the shared git executor classifies git remote), the set-url fallback and the add of the fork as origin (fork, remote, held against the fork clone URL they point origin at) and set-head -a (clone, remote, the fetch class, against the fork). Each step first re-reads the remote it acts on and refuses when it no longer names what the setup expects (origin, then upstream, is the cloned URL; origin is the fork before set-head), so a remote changed across the awaits is never renamed or overwritten. Both callers (symphony-runner startContribution and the symphony:start / startContribution handlers) wire it. cancelContribution holds the remote branch deletion (--delete-branch) as its own push effect against origin, after the cancel and before gh pr close; a refusal of either leaves the PR, branch and clone untouched. The runner clone cleanup is a local-effects delete (SymphonyRepositoryGate.localEffects), held right before fs.rm, of the folder handle read after the clone (or at the start of cancel) only; a refused or moved cleanup is left in place and reported. No published operation delivers the repository or local-effects ceiling (proposed, not negotiated): an enrolled desktop with none refuses these effects unavailable by name.
extensionProposals.symphonyCloneCleanup: MCOMP-21-11 holds every desktop Symphony clone removal as a destructive local delete by itself, never as part of the repository effect that led to it. symphony:start reads the clone handle (lstat device and inode) right after git clone and every failed later step (a refused branch, a failed branch, a failed or refused fork, a failed draft PR) removes the clone through removeClone (src/main/ipc/handlers/symphony/shared.ts): holdDeleteOfHandles holds delete against the calling transport immediately before the removal and compares the handle again, so a refused delete or a path swapped across the awaits is left in place and logged. symphony:cancel with cleanup reads the handle BEFORE isContributionClone awaits git, holds the delete after the cancel hold (cancel grants no delete; the cleanup flag widens nothing) and answers cleanupProblem when the clone stays. Standalone (no local-effects ceiling) both removals are the plain fs.rm they were. The ceiling reaches the handlers through SymphonyHandlerDependencies.getLocalEffectAuthority. No published operation delivers the local-effects ceiling (proposed, not negotiated).
extensionProposals.litePeerEgressClass: MCOMP-21-12A adds the closed egress class lite-peer (EGRESS_CLASSES in src/main/enterprise/egress-policy.ts), a versioned Maestro-local extension of the egress ceiling: no published ceiling names it, so a managed host whose policy does not list it sends no Lite peer bytes. The pairing transport (pairingTransport().call in src/main/lite/pairing/transport.ts), whose request leaves through node:http / node:https rather than fetchWithTimeout, holds the pairing origin with holdEgress() as lite-peer before the LAN or tailnet destination is resolved and again after that await, right before request() opens the socket, so a revocation in between sends nothing; a refusal rejects as the [managed-...] EgressDeniedError and is recorded in the hold ledger, never reported as a transport error. Standalone (no egress authority) nothing is consulted and pairing leaves exactly as before. The paired relay (openPairedRelay in src/main/lite/tailnet-relay.ts, MCOMP-21-12B) holds the paired origin as lite-peer after its ssh-tunnel listener hold and before the first destination read, and again on every relayed HTTP request and every WebSocket upgrade after the shared destination await and right before request() opens the upstream socket; the upstream is built only from the selected paired origin (any other origin is refused, no alternate peer route). A refusal answers the request 403 or destroys the upgrade socket, sends nothing upstream and stops the relay, closing every tracked socket (open WebSockets included). No published operation delivers an egress ceiling, so lite-peer is refused unavailable on an enrolled host until one is negotiated.
extensionProposals.standardProviderPermissionArgs: MCOMP-21-13 replaces the full-access batch arguments of a STANDARD turn with a qualified bounded combination where one was verified against an exact provider version (standardModeArgs and standardModeVerifiedVersion on the provider definition, src/shared/maestro-lib/providers/definitions.ts): codex 0.167.0 exec --sandbox workspace-write; gemini-cli 0.67.0 --approval-mode auto_edit (its policy engine denies, never asks, in a non-interactive run); grok 1.0.77 --permission-mode acceptEdits --deny Bash(*) (a denied rule never prompts, a cancelled headless prompt kills the turn). buildAgentArgs (src/shared/maestro-lib/launch/agent-args.ts) strips the full-access flags and appends the combination when standard is asked for by name or held to a ceiling; a legacy launch that names no mode is byte for byte what it was. antigravity 1.5.3 (headless soft-denies shell and stalls without its bypass flag), qwen3-coder, hermes, factory-droid and copilot-cli (no installed version to verify) have NO qualified standard mode: under a ceiling a standard batch turn for them is refused by name (ManagedPermissionModeError) instead of launching with the bypass flag dropped. No readonly mode was added: none was executed against its enforcement. supportsStandardPermissionMode stays false for all of them, so the UI still offers no standard mode; positive available functionality waits for provider route qualification (QUAL-01). Maestro-local behavior, no wire operation.
extensionProposals.agentMutation: MCOMP-23-01 adds the one host create/edit check for governed agent fields. checkManagedAgentMutation (src/shared/maestro-lib/managed/agent-policy.ts) validates, by value, a create/clone/import (every governed kind) or an edit (the kinds that change, parents still matched) against the ManagedAgentOptions read from live authority at the commit: options available with an applied revision, the expected form revision (stale otherwise), the operation listed, and each provider, model, account, workspace, credential, permission and transport value resolving from an approved reference whose parent (provider; account for a credential) is itself matched, within the field bounds. Refusals are typed (unavailable, stale, operation, field) and name each field. authorizeManagedAgentCommand (src/main/agents/agent-config-writes.ts) is the desktop command: standalone admits as before without reading options, a managed standing reads options per call and fails closed when standing, options or resolution cannot be read; managedAgentRepositoryAuthority composes it into the new AgentRepositoryOptions.authorizeAgentMutation hook, which createAgent/updateAgent consult inside the command queue with the record exactly as it would be committed. Approved choices commit (no blanket managed refusal). Missing: ManagedAgentRefResolver.version=1, the host-only resolution of an approved opaque reference to the value a record carries (provider id, model, working directory, account digest, credential ref id, permission mode, transport). No published operation delivers it, so no production resolver is installed and a managed mutation is unavailable by name until DESKTOP-LOCAL/1 is negotiated. Routing desktop whole-record persistence and the New/Edit Agent forms through this command is MCOMP-23-02..04; no wire operation or capability is advertised. MCOMP-23-02 composes it on the desktop (setAgentMutationAuthority in src/main/index.ts: standing from identityStandingOf, options from PolicyStatusService.agentOptions, account digest from the stored layers, resolver null) and routes every whole-record write through it: sessions:commitAgent (src/main/ipc/handlers/persistence.ts) is the one validated create/edit/clone/import operation returning the canonical record or a typed refusal; sessions:setMany, sessions:setAll and the plugin store path put a refused edit's governed fields back and never persist a refused new record. With no resolver an enrolled host answers unavailable by name; no external capability is advertised.
extensionProposals.newAgentForm: MCOMP-23-03 adapts the New Agent form (src/renderer/components/NewInstanceModal/NewInstanceModal.tsx) to the host's approved choices. useManagedAgentOptions (src/renderer/hooks/enterprise/useManagedAgentOptions.ts) now also reports managed (any enrolled standing), standing and policySource from the same managed-state projection. On a managed desktop the form shows the policy revision, its source (endpoint, installed copy offline, none) and freshness, a Refresh policy control, each governed field's approved opaque references and why a field is fixed, or why approved choices are unavailable; a standalone (unenrolled) desktop renders nothing new and keeps its normal editable form. Create awaits the host commit (one at a time; the form closes only on success), sends the revision the form was built from as onCreate's trailing policy argument, keeps the draft on any refusal, lists the host's per-field reasons (the working-directory reason also sits on that input) and refreshes approved choices after a stale refusal. References never enter the environment editor or any record field. Missing (DESKTOP-LOCAL/1): a renderer-safe presentation of an approved reference (display label, or the provider/model it stands for); the projection carries opaque references only and resolution is host-only, so the form cannot yet narrow the provider picker or model list to approved values, and the host check at commit stays the only enforcement. Threading the revision from createNewSession into the commit is continuation MCOMP-23-03A. No wire operation or capability is advertised.
extensionProposals.editAgentForm: MCOMP-23-04 adapts Edit Agent (src/renderer/components/NewInstanceModal/EditAgentModal.tsx) and the shared provider settings panel (src/renderer/components/shared/AgentConfigPanel.tsx) to the same approved-choice and host-save model. Edit Agent shows ManagedChoicesNotice (revision, source, freshness, approved references, Refresh policy) on a managed desktop and nothing new standalone; a save the host refuses (AgentCommitRefusedError from the sessions:commitAgent edit) keeps the dialog open with its draft, lists the reasons by field ('Not saved'), puts the working-directory reason on that input and refreshes approved choices after a stale refusal; any other failure is reported as before. Before saving it says what a provider or working-directory change does to messages already queued. AgentConfigPanel reads the managed setting locks (settingsStore managedLocks) and renders a held agentConfig.customPath, customArgs (and the OpenCode agent field stored in it), customEnvVars, model or reasoningEffort section as a disabled fieldset with the policy's reason, so no create or edit surface offers a raw path, argument, environment, model or effort override that holdAgentRecordWrite would refuse. Missing (DESKTOP-LOCAL/1), as for newAgentForm: approved references are opaque and host-resolved, so the dialog cannot narrow the provider or model pickers to approved values; the host check at commit stays the enforcement. Sending the edit form's policy revision with the edit commit is continuation MCOMP-23-04A; the Symphony agent creation dialog (src/renderer/components/AgentCreationDialog.tsx) is continuation MCOMP-23-04B. No wire operation or capability is advertised.
extensionProposals.symphonyAgentCreation: MCOMP-23-04B adapts the Start Symphony agent dialog (src/renderer/components/AgentCreationDialog.tsx) to the approved-choice model of newAgentForm and editAgentForm. It shows ManagedChoicesNotice on a managed desktop (nothing new standalone) and sends AgentCreationConfig.expectedPolicyRevision (the revision its approved choices came from, null standalone). SymphonyModal (src/renderer/components/SymphonyModal/SymphonyModal.tsx) carries it as SymphonyContributionData.expectedPolicyRevision and now awaits onStartContribution, typed in SymphonyModal/types.ts as void | Promise<SymphonyContributionOutcome | void>, before it closes the dialog; an outcome { ok: false, error, refusal } returns to the dialog as AgentCreationResult { success: false, error, refusal }, which keeps the draft, lists the reasons by field ('Not created'), puts a workspace reason under the working directory and refreshes approved choices after a stale refusal. Not yet done (continuation MCOMP-23-04C): the App's handler useSymphonyContribution still commits without the revision, toasts its own refusal and resolves nothing, and its prop type in AppStandaloneModals.tsx is still Promise<void>; and the contribution (clone, branch, fork, documents) is started BEFORE the agent commit, so a refusal leaves that clone behind with no active contribution to cancel. Missing (DESKTOP-LOCAL/1), as for newAgentForm: approved references are opaque and host-resolved, so the provider picker cannot be narrowed to approved values; the host check at commit stays the enforcement. No wire operation or capability is advertised.

extensionProposals.version: local delivery extension for content schema 1
extensionProposals.operations: Propose content_capture, content_upload_status and content_revoke at the endpoint; central HTTP upload definitions already exist.
extensionProposals.missing: Signed role/representation/sensitivity permissions, registration/run/policy binding, bounded chunk digest and residency, upload reference, durable acceptance, deletion/revocation and lost-response status. Pending bytes never imply uploaded evidence.

extensionProposals.version: local delivery extension for deviceInboxRecovery schema 1
extensionProposals.operations: Propose inbox_recover over the local endpoint; central deviceInboxRecoveryInput/Result already exist.
extensionProposals.missing: Registration-bound campaign/message/idempotency/requestDigest lookup and receipt custody; missing/unbound returns unavailable. No actor selector or automatic replay of private replies.

extensionProposals.version: protected independent headless identity custody extension; protocol/package version to be agreed
extensionProposals.operations: No public local operation delegates protected identity custody to a Node host. Propose an authenticated endpoint-owned host identity/custody binding; no speculative operation is sent.
extensionProposals.missing: Bind installation/runtime/process epoch and verified OS peer to an independently protected enrollment, freshness/rollback anchor, revocation and authenticated release. Never export Electron safeStorage keys, copy bearer credentials, or interpret schema imports as native support. Maestro uses the existing SealProvider/AnchorStore and EndpointPort when protected custody is supplied; default Node remains unavailable.

extensionProposals.version: local delivery extension for an enterprise detection (scan) requirement on third-party Cue input; protocol/package version to be agreed
extensionProposals.operations: No public operation or policy capability tells a managed host whether scanning third-party Cue input (GitHub issue/PR text, webhook deliveries) is optional enrichment or mandatory, nor which scorer, destination or credential it must use. capabilityRequirement.mandatory in the pinned policy schema names no such capability. Propose a signed, revisioned detection requirement inside the desktop policy batch; no speculative operation is sent and no capability is advertised.
extensionProposals.localConsumer: MCOMP-21-02 adds the typed port setSusFactorScanPolicy / SusFactorScanRequirement (optional | required with a reason) in src/main/cue/cue-susfactor.ts. Optional keeps the standalone fail-open contract. Required never fails open: an item with third-party text reaches an agent only after a completed scoring below the threshold; a refused custody or egress, a missing token, an upstream failure, a policy read error or susfactor_enabled: false holds the item by name and records no block. The headless Cue engine installs buildStandaloneCueSusFactorScanPolicy: standalone optional, any managed standing required, because with no delivered requirement a managed host cannot know scanning is optional. The desktop installs no scan policy (optional, unchanged).
extensionProposals.missing: The requirement itself (optional vs mandatory, per source), the approved scorer destinations and credential reference, threshold bounds, and an operator override rule under a mandatory requirement. Until delivered a managed headless engine holds every scorable item it cannot score, which with the egress ceiling also undelivered is every scorable item.

localTestBoundary.inputs: Required verified extracted contracts and exact Zod dependency; absence/tampering fails before schema loading.
localTestBoundary.cases: Public exports/ports/tasks, unsupported version/operation, forged actor/fleet purpose, actual transport replay, expired registration with fresh policy, endpoint denials, lost execution response with no retry, receipt versus permit, absent effect authority; existing public facade conformance remains exercised.
localTestBoundary.limits: Endpoint is a declared local double; denial parsing is not policy enforcement. No provider process, signed production policy, live actor authentication or paired/native security receipt. MCOMP-13-01 removes the broker-receipt-to-local-lease path. Prepared local tests inject an explicit authority; production prepared/per-effect wire mapping and all paired/native proof remain pending.
